root_cause.text: A copy-paste error in the USB audio descriptor validator table assigned the wrong protocol version (UAC_VERSION_2 instead of UAC_VERSION_3) for the UAC3 AC header descriptor entry, causing UAC3 header descriptors to bypass validation and enabling out-of-bounds reads from a maliciously truncated descriptor.
root_cause.evidence: The patch corrects line 284 in sound/usb/validate.c from `FIXED(UAC_VERSION_2, UAC_HEADER, struct uac3_ac_header_descriptor)` to `FIXED(UAC_VERSION_3, UAC_HEADER, struct uac3_ac_header_descriptor)`, and the commit message explicitly states that this wrong version causes the validator to never match for actual UAC3 devices (protocol == UAC_VERSION_3), leaving their header descriptors unvalidated.

    ALSA: usb-audio: More validations of descriptor units
    
    Introduce a new helper to validate each audio descriptor unit before
    and check the unit before actually accessing it.  This should harden
    against the OOB access cases with malformed descriptors that have been
    recently frequently reported by fuzzers.

bic_trace_step.reason: The code shows the audio_validators table entry for UAC3 AC header descriptor uses UAC_VERSION_2 (line: FIXED(UAC_VERSION_2, UAC_HEADER, struct uac3_ac_header_descriptor)), which is a copy-paste error; it should be UAC_VERSION_3. This causes UAC3 header descriptors to not match any validator (since protocol UAC_VERSION_2 != UAC_VERSION_3), so validation falls through and returns true even for malformed descriptors, enabling out-of-bounds reads. The fix (correct protocol) is not present.
